Spec-driven development

The harness is documentation and configuration: Markdown contracts, agent and skill definitions, and bash scripts that enforce them. There is no application runtime.

  • The specification leads. PRD.md states intent; SPECS.md decomposes it into epics and stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria.
  • One story, one change. Each story becomes its own OpenSpec change under openspec/changes/, never an epic-sized one.
  • Files are the state. Every handoff is a file in the change directory, so a fresh session resumes without chat history.
  • Gates are mechanical. Hooks run scripts that block an action whose preconditions are unmet. A rule that lives only in a prompt can be ignored.

Separation of duties

The Implementer never approves its own work. The Reviewer and the Tester report defects; they do not repair them. A blocked verdict is a successful verdict.

Getting started: every workflow

Where you start depends on two facts: whether the repository already has meaningful code, and whether a PRD.md exists. Every path ends at the same place: a SPECS.md backlog of READY stories.

Backlog already ready
SPECS.md has READY stories		skip straight to /product-iteration <US-N.M> or /deliver <target>.already recorded—
No product source at all/generate-prd and /ingest-spec stop and report that they need a source.—existing code is never turned into product intent
  • Code arrives later. A greenfield repository that gains code must run /analyze-codebase before its next PRD or SPECS update; the preflight guard blocks that update until it does.
  • Authority order. A human Product Manager decision, then approved product sources, then the existing PRD.md, then CODEBASE.md as evidence only.
  • This repository is greenfield: PRD.md and SPECS.md both record CODEBASE Context: absent.

The .claude harness, piece by piece

Claude Code reads .claude/: agents, skills, commands, rules, and hook settings. The hooks run the bash scripts in scripts/. Prompts say what an agent should do; hooks and guards decide what it can do.

Harness building blocks, counted from the repository.
KindWhereCountWhat it is
Agents.claude/agents/*.md8one role each: a prompt, a tool allow-list, and optionally a hook. Run as subagents through the Agent tool.
Skills.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md169 harness procedures, invoked as slash commands, plus 7 OpenSpec skills generated by the OpenSpec CLI
Commands.claude/commands/opsx/*.md7the /opsx:* change lifecycle, generated by openspec update
Rules.claude/rules/*.md7durable contracts that bind every session; each has a guard behind it
Hooks.claude/settings.json, agent frontmatter8 + 3Claude Code events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) wired to scripts
Guardsscripts/guard-*.sh, check-write-scope.sh6scripts that exit 2 to block a tool call or a stop
Validatorsscripts/validate-*.sh7artifact contracts: plan, review, test report, status, completion, product artifacts, HTML pages
Reportersworkflow-status.sh, completion-gate.sh, status.sh, delivery.sh4derive gate state, archive eligibility, durable state, and the next action
Suitesscripts/test-*.sh6regression suites for the scripts themselves

The delivery loop

/deliver drives one target story by story. The next action is derived by scripts/delivery.sh next on every turn, never remembered.

The delivery loop is a senior developer's tooling

A senior developer carries a delivery discipline in their head: slice the work, plan before coding, get it reviewed, test against the requirement, never ship with open issues, and ask when the decision is not theirs. The loop turns each habit into a mechanism that runs whether or not anyone remembers it.

Habit to mechanism, from .claude/skills/deliver/SKILL.md, .claude/rules/delivery-loop.md, and scripts/delivery.sh.
The senior habitThe loop's mechanism
pick the next unblocked piece of workdelivery.sh next walks SPECS.md in order, checking readiness and dependencies, and derives one action
slice an epic into shippable piecesone story = one OpenSpec change; a task delivers its parent story with the task as the Focus
don't start coding without a planguard-planning-handoff.sh blocks product-code writes until implementation-plan.md exists
get a second pair of eyesthe Reviewer subagent writes review.md; the orchestrator is blocked from writing it
test against the requirement, not the codethe Tester subagent scores every Gherkin scenario in test-report.md; UNVERIFIED is never PASS
fix findings, then re-checkdelivery.sh reopen preserves the verdict in history/, appends one task per finding, and re-opens review and test
never merge with open issuescompletion-gate.sh checks four conditions; guard-archive.sh refuses openspec archive until all pass
don't call it done earlyguard-story-done.sh refuses Status: DONE before the archive
finish what you startedthe Stop hook refuses to end the turn while the goal is ACTIVE and names the next action
leave a trailevery artifact stays in the change directory and moves to openspec/changes/archive/; a fresh session resumes from files
know when to askthe escalate action stops the loop and records BLOCKED with the decision needed

When the loop asks a human

The seven escalation causes in scripts/delivery.sh:

  1. the story is not READY: a product decision is required;
  2. the story depends on an unfinished story;
  3. another change is already active: one at a time;
  4. the gate reporter could not report;
  5. an artifact contract fails the acceptance gate;
  6. every gate passes but a completion condition fails;
  7. the first incomplete gate is one the loop does not know.

The human stays the Product Manager

The loop does the routine: selection, sequencing, delegation, bookkeeping. People decide scope, answer escalations, and own product intent. A loop that could approve its own work would turn "keep going until done" into "declare done", so it cannot.

Worked example: delivering EPIC-12 through Claude

EPIC-12 built the delivery loop, and then the loop delivered the rest of the epic. After US-12.1 was archived, the goal was recorded with scripts/delivery.sh start EPIC-12, and every later step followed scripts/delivery.sh next (SPEC-LOGS/README-EPIC-12.md §5). Claude Code 2.1.128, OpenSpec 1.13.2.

The four EPIC-12 changes, read from their archived artifacts.
StoryArchived changeTasksReview roundsFinal reviewScenariosCapabilities
US-12.12026-09-24-us-12-1-resolve-delivery-target-report153approved6/6delivery-target
US-12.22026-09-26-us-12-2-run-delivery-goal-loop172pass6/6delivery-loop
US-12.32026-09-26-us-12-3-document-delivery-orchestrator101pass2/2harness-documentation
US-12.42026-09-26-us-12-4-delivery-loop-followups81pass4/4delivery-target harness-documentation

One story end to end: US-12.2, "Run the delivery goal loop"

  1. next → select. delivery.sh next derived select US-12.2. The Product Manager ran openspec new change us-12-2-run-delivery-goal-loop, set the story IN PROGRESS in SPECS.md (guard-story-done.sh allowed it), and wrote status.md with status.sh.
  2. propose. /opsx:explore then /opsx:propose produced proposal.md, design.md, specs/delivery-loop/spec.md with six scenarios, and tasks.md with thirteen tasks, each mapped to a scenario.
  3. plan. /plan-feature delegated to the planner subagent (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash only), which returned implementation-plan.md. validate-implementation-plan.sh passed, and gate 3 (plan-handoff) opened.
  4. implement. The main session built .claude/skills/deliver/SKILL.md, .claude/rules/delivery-loop.md, scripts/guard-delivery-loop.sh wired as a Stop hook and a PreToolUse verdict guard, and delivery.sh block. It ticked tasks 1.1–2.6. guard-planning-handoff.sh allowed the writes because the plan existed.
  5. review, round 1. The reviewer subagent, limited to review.md by check-write-scope.sh --role reviewer, passed the change with observations.
  6. follow-ups. The verdict was kept as history/review-r1.md, and R1.1–R1.4 were appended and implemented: loop.state cleared on every goal transition, an honest message when a halt cannot be recorded, documented verdict-guard limits, and fixed pluralisation. Code changed, so the change went back to review instead of being archived.
  7. review, round 2. Pass, 17/17 tasks, OpenSpec verify: VERIFIED.
  8. test. The tester subagent built its own sandbox (mktemp -d /tmp/tst-us122.XXXXXX) and scored 6/6 scenarios PASS in test-report.md.
  9. archive. completion-gate.sh --record wrote completion.md with verdict eligible; openspec archive us-12-2-run-delivery-goal-loop -y passed guard-archive.sh and created openspec/specs/delivery-loop/.
  10. mark-done, then next. SPECS.md got Status: DONE and the archive path. delivery.sh refresh recomputed the goal, and next derived select US-12.3. US-12.3 and US-12.4 followed the same steps, and the last next returned complete.

Delivery goal EPIC-12 is ACTIVE — do not stop yet.

The Stop-hook message is the format documented in .claude/skills/deliver/SKILL.md Step 3, which uses this step as its example. The whole epic ran as:

select US-12.2 -> propose -> plan -> implement -> review -> (follow-ups) -> review
-> test -> archive -> mark-done -> select US-12.3 -> propose -> plan -> implement -> ...

Known limits, recorded in README-EPIC-12 §7

Live Claude Code behavior (the hook firing, the 8-block override) was not exercised in a live session. The verdict guard sees only Write, Edit, and MultiEdit, not shell redirects. The main session implemented this harness-on-harness epic, and independence came from delegating planning, review, and testing to separate subagents.

Artifacts and handoffs

Roles never pass messages. Each writes a file that the next role reads, and a gate checks the file exists and is well formed.

Hooks and guards

Claude Code runs the hooks declared in .claude/settings.json. Each hook runs a script; a script that exits 2 blocks the tool call or the stop.

Exit-code contract

  • Validators: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 usage error.
  • Guards: 0 allow, 2 block, 3 usage error.
  • Every hook wrapper fails open when the harness script is absent.
